evals.prompt: I already have VSS deployed in search mode and reachable at `http://10.10.1.20:12345`. I want the VSS MCP server running so Claude Desktop can call the VSS search tools. How do I start it, and exactly what URL and transport should I configure in Claude Desktop?
evals.expected_output: Explains the MCP server comes up with the VSS deployment (source setup.sh <mode>) and connecting via Streamable HTTP at http://<HOST_IP>:12345/mcp (proxied by the nginx gateway).
expectations: Uses the real start path: `source setup.sh <mode>` (e.g. `make deploy-search`) from the app root - the MCP server runs with the stack and needs no separate start step.
States HOST_IP is the only required setting and VSS_IP defaults to it (set only when VSS runs elsewhere); does not invent API_SPEC_URL, FILTER_FILE_PATH, search.json or mcp/.env.
Gives the endpoint http://<HOST_IP>:12345/mcp (via the nginx gateway) with the Streamable HTTP transport, not stdio.
Notes the tool surface follows GET /app/features, so a search-mode deployment exposes search tools but no summary tools.
Includes a verification step such as calling vss_get_deployment_info, checking `docker logs vss-mcp-server`, or probing /manager/health.

evals.prompt: I'm changing code under `mcp/src` and want to poke at the tools in MCP Inspector. VSS is up on `192.168.1.50`. Does the VSS stack give me Inspector? If not, what's the quickest way to get it?
evals.expected_output: Explains the VSS stack never starts Inspector, but mcp/compose.yaml's standalone mcp-inspector service does, with one command and no need to stop VSS.
expectations: States that the VSS stack (docker/compose.mcp.yaml, profile mcp) runs only the MCP server and never MCP Inspector.
Gives the standalone command from mcp/: `HOST_IP=192.168.1.50 docker compose up -d mcp-inspector` (no need to stop VSS first).
Says to open http://<HOST_IP>:6274, choose Streamable HTTP, and connect to http://<HOST_IP>:12345/mcp (the running deployment's own MCP server via the nginx gateway).

For testing an uncommitted code change specifically, mentions the optional mcp-server service in the same file builds a separate vss-mcp-server-dev container on its own host port (default 8001), distinct from the deployment's vss-mcp-server container, so both can run at once.
States Inspector auth is on by default (a token is printed in `docker compose logs mcp-inspector`) and that DANGEROUSLY_OMIT_AUTH=true should only be used on a trusted network.

evals.prompt: I want the VSS MCP server to expose a new tool that returns a single video's metadata by id. Where do I add it and how do I make sure it only appears when it can work?
evals.expected_output: Explains that tools are hand-declared in mcp/src/tools, registered in register(), returning a projection, tested against FakeVss.
expectations: Says tools are hand-declared code in mcp/src/tools/*.py, not an OpenAPI filter entry; there is no search.json.
Describes registering with @mcp.tool inside the module's register(), with annotations such as readOnlyHint and a model-facing docstring.
Says to return a projection rather than the raw Pipeline Manager payload and keep listing results within the byte budget (cap_payload); search hits and summaries are not capped.
Mentions gating on deps.features when the tool needs search or summary.
Adds a test in mcp/tests/test_tools.py against FakeVss and runs `poetry run python -m pytest -q tests` from mcp/.

evals.prompt: My agent is connected to the VSS MCP server but `vss_search_video` doesn't show up in the tool list. `vss_list_videos` works fine. What's going on?
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses the feature gate: search tools are only registered when GET /app/features reports search FEATURE_ON at startup.
expectations: Explains that search tools register only when GET /manager/app/features returns search: FEATURE_ON at MCP server startup.
Gives a concrete check: curl http://<VSS_IP>:12345/manager/app/features and/or vss_get_deployment_info (search_enabled).
Points at the server log startup line 'Deployment features: [...]' via docker logs vss-mcp-server or the dev stack logs.
Notes the feature set is read once, so the MCP server must be restarted after switching VSS to a search-capable mode.
Does not blame an OpenAPI filter, operationId or search.json.

evals.prompt: I'm developing against `mcp/src` directly and don't want to rebuild a Docker image every time. VSS is running at `192.168.1.50:12345`. How do I run the MCP server locally with Poetry, and which environment variables do I actually need?
evals.expected_output: Gives the Poetry run from mcp/ with HOST_IP (and optionally VSS_IP) and lists optional settings.
expectations: Runs from mcp/: `poetry install` then `HOST_IP=192.168.1.50 poetry run mcp-app` (entry point src.main:main).
States HOST_IP is the only required variable; VSS_IP/APP_HOST_PORT default to HOST_IP/12345.
Lists relevant optional settings from src/core/config.py such as MCP_PORT, MCP_PATH, LOG_LEVEL, REQUEST_TIMEOUT.
Explains the server probes /manager/app/features at startup and exits if VSS is unreachable.
Does not require API_SPEC_URL, API_BASE_URL, FILTER_FILE_PATH or a mcp/.env file.

evals.prompt: Why is there no upload tool in the VSS MCP server? My agent needs to get a video into VSS before it can search it.
evals.expected_output: Explains upload is deliberately not a tool and the upload_url flow from vss_get_deployment_info.
expectations: States that video upload is intentionally not an MCP tool.
Gives the reason: accepting file bytes over MCP is neither safe nor reliable, and a generic HTTP fetch tool would make the server an open proxy.
Tells the agent to call vss_get_deployment_info for upload_url (http://<VSS_IP>:<APP_HOST_PORT>/manager/videos) and POST multipart/form-data with field `video` outside MCP.
Says to pass the returned videoId to vss_index_video before searching.
Does not suggest adding POST /videos to a filter file.

evals.prompt: Our UI will let users attach a photo and ask Hermes to find similar moments in VSS. Passing base64 through MCP is too heavy. How should the image get to `vss_search_video`?
evals.expected_output: Explains the claim-check flow: upload via POST /manager/search/images, pass imageUrl/imagePath/imageId as `image`, Pipeline Manager reads from MinIO.
expectations: Describes uploading the image to POST /manager/search/images (multipart field `image`, jpg/jpeg/png/webp, max 2 MB) and getting back imageId/imageUrl/imagePath.
Says to pass that reference as the `image` argument of vss_search_video, which forwards it as imageUrl; no image bytes cross MCP and the MCP server fetches nothing.
Notes arbitrary external URLs are rejected (400) by design, as SSRF protection; only images in the upload bucket are accepted.
Notes image search needs a frame-embedding mode (--search or --dual) and exactly one of query or image.
Mentions cleanup with DELETE /manager/search/images/{imageId}.
